success_criterion: AGENTS.md 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline'
question: On E0/F_2^19 (EC1N19Ckb1h01617b86df6c, r = 130873), does running the whole tau6 index calculus in native code (setup, target draws, point arithmetic, shift loop, relation checks, GF(r) left kernel and log: candidate N2, no Sage process) lower the end-to-end cold CPU cost of one complete, verified ECDLP against the current n = 19 row (arm N of volcano-n19-native-tau6-v3-20261020: Sage tauDlp with the native per-shift solve), with every target, shift order, shift system, relation, matrix, kernel and log unchanged?

current_baseline.row: arm N of volcano-n19-native-tau6-v3-20261020 (PR #1005, run 39387473809): Tier 1, cold CPU B / N 141.02 [136.75, 144.95], cold S 31.42 in that run's rho unit

curve.generator: run.sage generator(cur, "E0"); must equal the archived P of runtime-info.json

change.what: native/ (crate tau6-loop): tau6dlp runs TauCurve, generator, tauEigen and tauDlp natively; the per-shift solve is the v3 source file included by path (byte-identical source)
kept_exactly: V' base, orbit representatives (smallest encoding; y as Sage lift_x: the smaller encoding, fixed by the archived relations of all 29 columns and the archived P), base table
generator: random.Random('gen:E0') draws, lift_x(x, all=True)[0], cofactor 4
targets: CPython MT19937 random.Random(seed) randrange(1, r) twice, R = al P + be Q, skip if zero; shuffle of the one persistent shift list
per shift: the v3 variety in Sage's order; spurious counting; sign order (1,1), (1,-1), (-1,1), (-1,-1); first hit returns

rows column -> sum sign lambda^e (insertion order), rhs (4 al, 4 be) mod r, used columns sorted, left kernel in reduced echelon form (Sage's basis), first vector with B != 0, s = -A / B, verified s P == Q
change.not_timed_per_call: N2 records gb_cpu_s = null: reading the process clock around each of about 5,000 solves would cost a sizeable share of N2's own interval

arms.N: baseline: v3 arm.sage --arm N (Sage process), v3 library
arms.N2: candidate: tau6dlp --arm N2 (native process, no Sage)
arms.N2aa: A/A control: a second process of N2 (tau6dlp --arm N2aa)
arms.N2X: planted positive control: arm_n2x.sage: N2's pipeline through libtau6loop.so plus arm N's whole Sage path and Sage's left kernel on the same point, compared item by item (abort on any difference)
arms.B: v3 arm B (Sage Groebner, the v3 baseline): one process per point, correctness and the chain secondary B / N2
arms.rho: v3 arm rho (matched signed-Frobenius rho), for the S unit and the gap
arms.warm: one N2 process per point with --warm (repeated-batch secondary), unpaired
arms.gates: selftest (S0, v3 arm on libtau6loop.so), S0b (binary), O (v3 arm O, baseline), O2 (binary)

design.panel: inputs/panel.json (role n19-native-loop-heldout, make_panel.py, seed volcano-n19-native-loop-20261021:panel): 24 new scalars, none equal to, the negative of or a Frobenius image of an archived scalar, of a v1, v2 or v3 panel scalar, or of each other
design.rng: tauDlp rng = random.Random(point rng_seed) in every IC process of a point
design.schedule: schedule.json (make_schedule.py), part timed: S0, S0b, O1, O2, then Q01..Q24; per point a seeded (volcano-n19-native-loop-20261021:order:%d) start for each paired block and a shuffled order of the primary, A/A, planted, B, rho and warm blocks; strict alternation inside each paired block
design.smoke: schedule.json part smoke (untimed gate): S0, S0b, O1, O2, v3 points p00 and p01 through B, N, N2, N2aa, N2X, rho and warm N2; job sage-smoke; the timed job needs it and its artifacts
design.process_model: one fresh pinned process per run (sched_setaffinity to one CPU, the lowest allowed, before exec), one runner per part
design.environment: GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner; sagemath/sagemath:10.10@sha256:310dfe23fc786f3a5a06a7b0387c60201ec79b32c0db941b7624505ee5edb565 (the baseline run's image); native library built on the runner by the pinned Rust toolchain before the schedule; the tau6dlp binary and libtau6loop.so built the same way
design.time_guard: part timed: before each segment, skip it and every later one (rows skipped_time_guard, verdict invalid) if elapsed job time + max(segment upper estimate, 1.1 x longest point segment so far) exceeds 175 min; a failed gate stops the part before any timed row; job timeout 200 min
design.workflow: .github/workflows/n19-native-loop.yml (workflow_dispatch; push trigger limited to branch claude/n19-native-loop and the frozen, non-report paths of this experiment)
design.runtime_estimate: smoke job about 15 min; timed job about 35 min (gates 2 min; per point B 35-65 s, 5 N about 1.5 s each, N2X about 2 s, rho 1.7 s, 11 N2/N2aa processes well under 1 s each: about 65 s; 24 points about 26 min); worst case B at 100 s about 50 min; with queueing and image pulls about 1-1.5 h in all, inside the 3 h budget

isolation_records: scripts/host_cpu_record.py at start and end (model, microcode, flags, caches, topology, kernel, THP)
scripts/isolated_bench.py host probe, cgroup counters and tier1 noise gate per run (throttling, memory events, steal, interrupts, thermal, major faults)
placement: Cpus_allowed_list / Cpus_allowed from /proc/<pid>/status and the arm's sched_getaffinity
scheduling: /proc/schedstat line of the execution CPU and /proc/stat ctxt, procs_running, procs_blocked, CPU line, before and after each run
getrusage of the child: user and system CPU, voluntary and involuntary switches, minor and major faults, peak RSS
allocation.json: provider, instance id, runner, image, CPU model, memory, THP, git sha, run URL

intervals.clock: process CPU time: time.process_time() in Sage arms, clock_gettime(CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID) (the clock behind time.process_time) in tau6dlp; wall co-reported
intervals.setup: target-independent construction: N as in v3 (NativeTauField, TauCurve, native context, generator); N2: Setup::new() (field tables, solve context, V' base, representatives, base table, generator)
intervals.online: tauDlp: tauEigen, targets, shift loop, rows, left kernel, log, s P == Q
intervals.cold: setup + online, one process, one point
intervals.fixture: Q = s * P between setup and online, outside both
intervals.outside: process start-up (Sage import and source loading for N; exec for N2), the post-interval field check and record writing are outside every interval of both arms; the launcher records them (launcher_wall_s, child CPU)

statistics.primary: R = sum over the 120 primary pairs of cold_cpu_s(N) / sum of cold_cpu_s(N2) (in-process cold CPU, the same intervals as v3's primary and the ledger's cold S)
statistics.primary_choice: In-process cold CPU is the primary because (1) it is the measure of the current row (v3 primary, ledger cold S in the rho unit, which is also in-process CPU), so the ratchet stays in one unit; (2) it is conservative for this candidate: it leaves out Sage start-up, which only N pays (about 1.2 s of child CPU per N process in run 39387473809, several times N's whole cold interval), so it can only understate N2's advantage; (3) start-up is a property of the interpreter, not of the algorithm, and is the same for any Sage arm whatever it computes.
statistics.process_inclusive_secondary: named, pre-registered: child CPU (user + system, getrusage of the launched process: start-up, intervals and post-interval work) N / N2 over the same 120 pairs, same bootstrap; reported with its own verdict label (improvement iff its lower bound > 1); it never changes the verdict. Launcher wall N / N2 is reported beside it
statistics.interval: two-stage paired bootstrap (points with replacement, then pairs within each drawn point; N and N2 of a pair together), 10,000 draws, random.Random(2026102101), 2.5% and 97.5% order statistics (stats.py)
secondary: geometric mean of pair ratios; online, setup, cold wall, child CPU and launcher wall N/N2
per-point ratios, ratio when N first / N2 first, ratio by pair position

mean per arm; S = cpu / (u sqrt(r)) per arm with u the rho CPU per group operation of this run; cold gap N2 / rho (geometric, bootstrap); chain B / N2 (one B per point over the point's mean N2, one-stage over points)
phase shares of N2 (setup, relation loop, linear algebra); warm batch means

decision_rule.improvement: R 95% lower bound > 1 (N2 becomes the n = 19 end-to-end cold baseline, Tier 1, this provider and host class)
decision_rule.invalid: any gate is false, missing or unknown, or a control fails

controls.aa: A/A: sum cold_cpu_s(N2) / sum cold_cpu_s(N2aa) over the 72 A/A pairs; pass iff the estimate is inside aa_window (the interval is reported)
controls.planted: R_plant = sum cold(N2X) / sum cold(N2) over the 24 planted pairs, same bootstrap: pass iff its 95% lower bound > 1

gates.receipt_rows_match_schedule: exactly one row per scheduled run and none unscheduled; serial, arm, point, role, pair, side, position, segment and the command line (executable, arm, serial, point, scalar, rng seed, --warm) equal the schedule; candidate arms ran the tau6dlp binary, baseline arms the v3 arm.sage under sage, N2X arm_n2x.sage
gates.rows_in_schedule_order: rows were written and finished in serial order
gates.every_scheduled_row_valid: every scheduled run ran (no time-guard skip, no stop), exit 0, row file written, no memory event, artifacts unchanged, arm reported correct
gates.raw_records_verified: each row's stdout raw_b64 record decodes, its SHA-256 equals the summary line's and the row file's bytes, and its serial, arm, point, scalar, rng seed and warm flag equal the schedule
gates.relation_digests_recomputed: every IC row's and every O1 / O2 instance's ordered, canonical and rows digests recompute from its raw relations (v3 relation_digest.py); N2X's native digest equals its Sage digest
gates.runner_identity_matches_frozen_files: runner_start / runner_end record this part and the SHA-256 of the frozen files and baseline sources (v3 arm, binding, digests, v3 native sources, tau.sage, run.sage, ic.sage, rho, archive), unchanged at the end
gates.schedule_and_panel_regenerate: schedule.json and inputs/panel.json regenerate byte for byte
gates.native_artifacts_one_digest: three distinct artifacts (v3 libtau6native.so, libtau6loop.so, tau6dlp), one digest each at start and end, before and after every run, and each process reports the digest of the artifact its arm uses
gates.placement_pinned_every_process: every child's Cpus_allowed_list and the arm's own sched_getaffinity are the one execution CPU
gates.host_cpu_identity_unchanged: host_cpu_record model, family, model, stepping, microcode and flags equal at start and end
gates.tier1_counters_recorded: isolated_bench counters and the execution CPU's /proc/schedstat line recorded before and after every run
gates.s0_passed: v3's S0 (2,982 systems: 7 v1 mismatch, v2's 300, v3's 300, all 2,375 multi-solution) on libtau6loop.so's tau6_* solve: Sage variety == native (as sets and in order) == brute force, direct S3 in Sage's field == native on the 607 non-multi systems
gates.s0_binary_passed: the tau6dlp binary's compiled solve on the same 2,982 systems (read from the S0 row) returns Sage's variety in Sage's order on every one
gates.o1_passed: baseline N on the ten archived scalars reproduces run 38520305068 (v3 arm O)
gates.o2_passed: N2 (binary) on the ten archived scalars and seeds: targets, gb_calls, spurious, relations and log equal run 38520305068's tau6 rows; relations_raw and digests equal the v3 O1 row of run 39387473809; P and lambda equal the archive
gates.field_check_every_native_process: every Sage process with a native library: v3 binding_check (modulus == Sage's F.modulus() == 854355, 256 products equal Sage's); N2X on both libraries; every binary process: the same 256-product sample (Python's Random('native_binding.check_field')), each product recomputed by the verifier with v3 pymul modulo 854355, and the binary's two arithmetics agree
gates.counts_and_log_identical_per_point: per point, every IC process (B, N, N2, N2aa, N2X, warm N2) has the same targets, gb_calls, spurious, relations and log, and log == scalar mod r
gates.relations_identical_per_point: per point, every IC process has the same rows, canonical and ordered digests, count, and byte-identical relations_raw (ordered decompositions)
gates.setup_identical_per_point: per point, every N2 process reports the same 29 orbit representatives as Sage's cur.reps in the N2X process (29 orbits, 33 V' points)
gates.planted_compared_every_item: every N2X compared every target (al, be, R, shift order, calls, decomposition), gb_calls == checked calls > 0, every relation, the 29 representatives, the 33 base entries, and Sage's full left-kernel echelon basis, with no mismatch
gates.generator_equals_archived: every IC process's generator equals the archived P
gates.rho_verified: every rho process verified 64 of 64 repetitions
gates.warm_batch_reproduced: every warm N2 process repeated its cold relations in the warm batch, and no other process ran one
gates.smoke_points_equal_v3_archive: smoke only: on v3 panel p00 and p01 every IC process equals run 39387473809's archived Sage B row (counts, log, relations_raw, digests)
gates.sage_smoke_gate_passed: the untimed smoke part (its own job, pinned image) passes every smoke gate, re-derived by the verifier from its raw rows, with the same three artifact digests

s0.note: v3's S0 systems unchanged (the v3 arm.sage selftest, seeds inside it); run on libtau6loop.so and, through S0b, on the tau6dlp binary

multiplicity: one primary statistic; every secondary is descriptive and never changes the verdict

model.statistic: ratio of sums, two-stage paired bootstrap

power.note: the expected effect is far above min_delta: the native solve was 15.4% of N's cold CPU in v3 run 39387473809 and N2 keeps that solve, so with the rest of N removed the ratio would be about 1 / 0.154 = 6.5 if the port cost nothing; locally (cloud VM, not timing evidence) N2 took about 60 ms per point, nearly all in the v3 solve. min_delta 1.10 is the smallest effect the design is sized to detect

tier: Tier 1 (AGENTS.md "CPU performance evidence tiers"): one fresh GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, one pinned exposed CPU, one fresh process per run, repeated alternating pairs, 95% paired lower bound; CPU-only; not isolab; one host class; not replayed. A container affinity mask records placement, not host-wide exclusivity
what_is_not_claimed: no advance in the exponent and no change of algorithm: the same relations, matrix and log (engineering)
the per-shift solve is unchanged (v3 source); its own cost is not addressed here
nothing about rho beyond the gap: the matched rho is v3's Python/Sage walk
the smoke part's times are never used
